HOOD, FREDERICK JAMES, M.R.C.V.S.—B. 1893; ed. George Heriot's Sch. and R. Vety Coll., Edinburgh; war serv., France, 1916-19; vety. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Dec., 1922.

HOODLESS, D. W., B.Sc.—B. 1887; ed. Sheffield Univ. and King's Coll., London; B.Sc. hon., Lond., 1910; Drew gold medal, mathematics, 1910; associateship of King's coll.; mast., H.M.S. "Worcester," 1911; asst. mast., Queen Victoria schl., Fiji, 1912; head mast., Lau Schl., 1915; J.P. for the colony, 1916; ag. head mast., Queen Victoria schl., 1918; ag. supt., schl., 1922; prov. mem. leg. coun., Nov., 1924; asst. dir., educ., 1927.

HOOGENHOUT, NICOLAAS MARAIS.—B. 1876; ed. Boys' High Schl., Wellington and Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; M.A. (mod. lang.), Univ. of Cape of Good Hope; Ph.D., Kaiser-Wilhelms-Universitat, Strasbourg (Alsace); prin., Krendrecht High Schl., Pretoria, 1904; vice-prin., Normal Coll., Pretoria, 1906; prin., ditto, 1921; rector, Transvaal Univ. Coll., Pretoria, 1925; dir., educ., Transvaal, 1928.

HOOKER, RICHARD SYMONDS.—B. 1885; ed. Bedford Gram. Schl. and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; M.A. (Cantab.); qualified in exam. for gen. consular service; passed lower standard exam. in Mende; asst. dist. commr., Sierra Leone, July, 1910; dist. commr., Jan., 1915; ag. prov. commr., N. Prov., Nov., 1920 to Aug., 1921 and from Sept., 1922; prov. commr., 1st Jan., 1926.

HOOPS, ALBERT LAUNCLOT.—B. 1876; ed. at King William's Coll. and Trinity Coll., Dublin; B.A., 1900; M.B., B.Ch., B.A.O., 1901; M.D. (stip. cond.) 1903; D.P.H., 1903; L.M., Rotunda, 1903; certif. honours, London Sch. of Trop. Med., 1904; served in S. African War as medical offr., 28th M.I., 1901-2 (severely wounded, ment. in desps., medal and four clasps); house surgeon, Penang, 1904; surg. capt., Penang vol.; ag. col. surg. req., Penang, June, 1906; seconded to organise medical and prison depts. in Kedah, Mar., 1906; state surg. and supt. of prisons in Kedah to Nov., 1920; ag. adviser to govt. of Kedah, Sept., 1906, to Apr., 1907, and from July to Oct., 1907; supt. of Indian immigra., Kedah, in addition to other duties, Oct., 1910; prot. of lab., Kedah, in addition, Nov., 1917; prin. civil med. offr., S. Stltmte., 23rd Nov., 1920; pres. coun., coll. of med., S'pore.; pres., S.S. and F.M.S. med. council; mem., leg. coun., S. Stltmte., 1st Jan., 1923; chmn., tuberculosi comittee, June to Aug., 1923; pres., 5th Congress of Far Eastern Assoc. of Trop. Med., Singapore, Sept., 1923.

HOPE, JAMES.—B. 1899; ed. Potchefstroom Coll., Transvaal and R.M.U., Sandhurst; gaz. 2nd lieut., K.O.S.B., 1918; Br.-Gen. Serv. and Victory medals; joined Swaziland serv., Sept., 1919; gaz. clk. to A.C. Hlatikulu; ag. mast., regir. and sheriff, 1923; con. clk. to treas., N. Rhodesia, June, 1925; clk., Bech. Prot., May, 1927; passed 3rd grade Swazi language exam., 1921; passed Cape civ. serv., lower law exam., 1922.

HOPKINS, J. G.—Asst. dist. commr., E.A.P., Mar., 1917.

HOPKINSON, CAPT. EMILIUS, C.M.G. (1922), D.S.O. (1900), M.A., M.B., B.Ch. (Oxon.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), F.Z.S.—B. 1869; ed. at Haileybury, Trin. Coll., Oxford, and St. Thomas's hosp., Lond.; late ophthalmic house surg., St. Thomas's hosp.; clinical asst., Royal Ophthalmic hosp., Moorfields; house surg., Radcliffe infirmary, Oxford; served in S. African war, 1900-1901, as surg.-capt., 15th batt., I.Y. (ment. in desps., Queen's Med., 4 clasps, D.S.O.); late surg.-lieut., Oxford I.Y.; med. offr., W.A.F.F., Gambia, 1901-1902; prot. med. offr., Gambia, 1903; travelling commr., South Bank prov., Gambia, 1912; travelling commr., North Bank Prov., Gambia, 1921; author of "Vocabulary of the Mandingo Language."

HOPKINSON, GEORGE FREDERICK.—B. 1894; cler. asst., post office, Br. Guiana, 1911; 6th cls. offr., cust., 1912; 5th cls. ditto, 1914; 4th cls. clk., treasy., 1920; 3rd cls. ditto, 1923; 3rd cls. clk., col. secretariat, 1925; 2nd cls. clk., ditto, 1926.

HOPPS, HERBERT DAVIDSON.—B. 1876; asst. foreman, Indian State Rly., 1903; foreman, 1919; E. African Forces, 1914-19; asst. loco. supt., Tanganyika Rlys., Oct., 1919.

HOFTON, REGINALD EDWARD, L.R.C.P. (Edin.), L.R.C.S. (Edin.), L.R.F.P. & S. (Glas.).—B. 1887; surg. probationer, R.N.V.R. (on active serv.), 1916-19; house surg., R. Infirmary, Edin., 1921; clin. asst., Grovesnor Hosp. for women, London, 1923; clin.-asst., London Lock Hosp., 1925; specialist in venereal diseases, Cyprus, July, 1927.

HORE-RUTHVEN, MAJOR-GEN. HON. SIR ALEXANDER GORE ARKWRIGHT, K.C.M.G. (1928), V.C. (1899), C.B. (1919), C.M.G. (1918), D.S.O. (1916).—B. 1872; ed. Rton; joined 3rd batt. Highland Light Infy., 1891; attd. Egyptian Army, Soudan, 1896; commanded Camel Corps detachment at battle of Gedaref and subsequent operns. (V.C., 4th cls. Osmanieh, English and Egyptian medics with clasp, three times ment. in desps.); sp. serv. offr., Somaliland, 1903-04; mily. sec., Viceroys of Ireland, 1905-06; mily. sec., gov.-gen., C'wealth of Australia, 1906; served European war, France and Gallipoli, 1914-18 (severely wounded, D.S.O. and bar, C.B., C.M.G., ment. in desps. five times); commanded Welsh Guards, 1920-24; commanded 1st Infy. Brig. (Guards); 1924-28; gov., S. Australia, 1928.

HORN, ARTHUR EDWIN, C.M.G. (1922), M.D., B.S.(Lond.); M.R.C.S.(Eng.); L.R.C.P.(Lond.); D.T.M. and H. (Cantab.); certif., Lond. Sch. of Trop. Med. (with distinctions).—Ed. at St. Mary's Hosp. and London Univ.; civil surg., 19th brigade field hosp., S. African field force, 1900-1901; apptd. to W. African medical staff, 1904 and has served in G. Coast, N. and S. Nigeria and Gambia; awarded Craggs research
prize for original research in trop. med. (London S.T.M.), 1908; recd. thanks of S. of S. for the Colonies for report on cerebro-spinal fever in Northern Territories of the G. Coast, 1908, and for report on sleeping sickness in the Volta River dist. of the G. Coast, 1910; seconded for special service at the C.O., 1910-12; personal ass't to the P.M.O., S. Nigeria, 1913; senr. med. offr. ad mem., exec. and leg. couns., Gambia, 1914-16; prim. civ. med. offr., German E. Africa, 1917-19; att'd. Rockefeller oomsn. for investigation of yellow fever in W. Africa, 1920; dir. med. and sany. services, Malaya, 1921-22; pres. elect for 5th Congress of Far Eastern Assoc. of Trop. Med., 1923; med. sec. to Col. Advisory Med. and Sany. Comtee. at C.O., 1923-24; junr. med. adviser to C.O., 1924; mem., exec. comtee. of Br. Empire Leprosy Relief Assoc.; fellow R. Soc'y. of Med.; R. Soc'y. Trop. Med.; author of "Health of Europeans in W. Africa," "Health of Europeans in E. Africa."

HORNBY, CAPT. HENRY EPTON, O.B.E., F.R.C.V.S., D.V.S.M.—B. 1890; ed. King's Coll. Schl. and R. Vety. Coll., London; lect. in bacteriology to S.E. Agr. Coll. (Univ. of London), 1912-13; vety. offr., N. Rhodesia, 1913-20; war serv., E. Africa, N. Rhodesia Rifles, 1914-17; S.A.V.C., 1917-19; ment. in desps.; studied physiology and pathology, Univ. Coll. Schl. of Trop. Med., London, Ecole de Medicine, Paris, and Vety. Research Lab., Pretoria; vety. pathologist, Tanganyika Territory, Feb., 1922.

HORNE, EDWARD BUTLER, O.B.E. (1928).—Ed. at Bedford Gram. Schl.; ast. coll'r., E. Africa Prot., 21st Apr., 1904; dist. comsnr., 1st Apr., 1909; offr.-in-charge, Masai res., May, 1923; senr. comsnr. (2nd class), Kenya, Jan., 1924; senr. comsnr., 1st grade, 1926.

HORNE, EDWIN NOEL.—B. 1902; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 4th May, 1920.

HORSBURGH, HARRY, A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1876; ed. Aske's Haberdasher's Company Schl.; C.A., Jan., 1908; ast. dir., min. of munitions, 1915; dep. contr., munitions disposal bd., 1919; dep. head, engnr. contracts, 1920; tech. ast., "Discovery Comte," 1923.

HORSLEY, BERNARD HILL.—B. 1890; European War, 1914-18; major, 8th (service) batt., K.O.Y.L.I.; D.S.O., M.C., desps.; dist. polit. offr., Somaliland, 1919; dist. comsnr., Somaliland, 1922.

HORSLEY, RICHARD.—B. 1893; ed. Cowley Gram. Schl., St. Helens; gen. fitter, P.W.D., Gold Coast, 13th Aug., 1919; instr. of metalwks., Accra tech. schl., 10th Apr., 1920; ag. prin., 1st Dec., 1920 to 22nd Mar., 1921; house mast., 6th Sept., 1922; head mast., junr. trade schl., 28th Apr., 1926.

HORWOOD, HON. SIR WM. HENRY, KT. BACH. (1904).—B. 1862; ed. at Bishop Feild Coll., St. John's; called to the bar, 1886; bencher of the law society, Newfoundland, 1891; Q.C., 1896; elected to the legislature, 1894; acted as col. sec. 1894-5; delegate from the Newfoundland govt. to the Ottawa conf., Apr., 1895, on the subject of confedn. with Canada; mem. of ex. coun., 1894-97; ag. atty.-gen., 1897; elected to legislature to represent Harbour Grace, 1897; apptd. by ch. just., with minister of just. to act in conjunction with judges as committee to amend rules and procedure, sup. court, 1899; minister of just. and atty.-gen., 1900; ex-officio mem. of ex. coun., and of treasy. board; acted as leader of govt. during sess. of 1901; and also in 1902; apptd. ch. just., July, 1902; administered govt., 1902, 1904, 1909, 1912, 1913, 1914; deputy gov., 1907, 1910; chrmn. of royal comsn. on Sealing Industry, 1918; pres., Newfild. centre of St. John Ambulance Assoctn.; chrmn. of comtee. for selection of non-combatants for service abroad; chrmn. of Newfild. fund for hospital cots for soldiers and sailors; representative on Peace Comsn. established under treaty between Great Britain and U.S.A., May, 1916.

HOSEGOOD, THOMAS WILLIAM HABOLD.—B. 1886; habmrn. and naval agt., St. Lucia, Feb., 1918; ast. habmrn., Hong Kong, Apr., 1927.

HOSKING, E. B.—B. 1890; ed. King's Schl., Canterbury and Wadham Coll., Oxford (class schl.); ast. dist. comsnr. E.A.P., Dec., 1913; dist. comsnr., Kenya, 1925.

HOUGHTON, H. E.—B. 1892; apptd. after compet. exam., olk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser. and assigned to the C.O., Apr., 1912; attached to office of high comsnr. for S. Africa, Nov., 1920; transf'd. to Basutoland serv., Nov., 1923.

HOW, DOUGLAS WALSHAM.—B. 1889; ed. Cheltenham Coll., London Matric.; Un. of S. Africa civ. serv. lower law exam.; Basutoland 2nd grade Sesuto exam.; clerical ast., Basutoland, 5th Oct., 1910; sub-inspr., Basutoland mtd. pol., 1st July, 1912; chief olk., master of ct. and regier., 1st July, 1917; served as 2nd lieut. with Royal Welsh Fusiliers in France, 1918; inspr. and staff offr., Basutoland mtd. pol., 1st July, 1919; dep. ast., comsnr., 1923.

HOWARD, HON. ERATOS EDWIN.—B. 1868; ed. Iroquois High Schl., Inverness Acad., and McGill Univ.; B.A., 1896; gold medallist in maths. and nat. philos.; B.C.L. (gold medallist) 1898; barrister; practised in Montreal, 1899-1919; called to the bar, Quebec, July, 1899; K.C., Sept., 1913; judge, superior ct., prov. of Quebec, 26th Sept., 1919; judge of ct. of King's Bench, 9th Aug., 1920; prof., civ. law, McGill Univ. and elective fellow of law faculty.

HOWARD, FREDERICK JAMES, O.B.E.—B. 1883; ed. at Bedford; 2nd divn. clk., W.O., June, 1901; 2nd ols. ast. acctnt., army acctn. dept., May, 1905; selected for advancement to higher grade of scale, 1st Nov., 1911; ag. 1st ols. ast. acctnt., Oct., 1914; ag. acctnt., Nov., 1916; 1st ols. ast. acctnt., 15th Dec., 1919; personal supernumy. appt. as acctnt., 1st Jan., 1921; serv. with min. of munitions as dir. from 1915, and with disposal and liquidation comsn. treas., as ast. contr. of deptl. finance until 1921; O.B.E., 1st Jan., 1918; ag. prin., old style, 1st Jan., 1920; ag. prin. C.O., 16th Sept., 1921; print., 27th Aug., 1928.

HOWARD, JOHN CURTOIS.—B. 1887; ed. Uppingham and Clare Coll., Camb. (exhibt.); called to the bar, Inner Temple, Jan., 1913; 2nd lieut., 4th Lincoln Regt., Mar., 1915; served in France, Jan., 1917 to July, 1920; legal adviser, G.H.Q., France, May, 1919 to July, 1920; pres. dist. ct., Cyprus, Aug., 1920; passed exam. in mod. Greek, Aug., 1921; ag. king's advoc., Nov., 1922 to Mar., 1923 and Ang., 1923; king's advoc., July, 1924; title altered to atty.-gen., May, 1925; joint compilers, 2nd vol., statute laws of Cyprus, 1923; solr.-gen., Nigeria, 1926.

HOWARD-FLANDERS, WILLIAM EDGAR.—B. 1894; ed. Mill Hill Schl. and Exeter Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1920; M.A., 1927; served with H.M. Forces, 1914-18; called to bar, M.T., 1923; mem., south-eastern circo. and cent. crim. ct.; mag., St. Vincent, June, 1927; ag. atty.-gen., Apr., 1928; income tax comsnr., 1928; mem., eduon. bd., 1928; ag. col. sec., July, 1928; atty.-gen., Sept., 1928.
HOWARTH, SAMUEL EDWARD JAMES.—Ed. at Buxton Coll., London; served in S. African War, Queen's and King's medals with five clasps; asst. Colony manager, field force canteens, O.R.C., Feb., 1902, to Mar., 1903; asst. acctnt., P.W.D., E. Africa Prot., 6th May, 1905; ch. acct., P.W.D., 1916.

HOWATSON, CHARLES WILLIAM, M.B., C.M. (Edin.).—B. 1861; dist. med. offr., Trinidad, 15th May, 1905.

HOWELL, ALLEYN GRAHAM.—B. 1871; 5th clk. corrpdg. branch, C.S.O., Barbados, 1890; 4th clk., 1892; 3rd clk., Jan., 1898; ch. clk. comsnr. of agriculture, 1899; sec. to W. Indian agric. conferences, 1900, 1901, 1902, 1905, and 1907.

HOWELL, E. H., M.B.E. (1927).—B. 1879; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser. and assigned to the C.O., Mar., 1898; promoted, with gratuity, Dec., 1907; conf. clk., 1911; staff clk., 1st grade, 8th Sept., 1917; deptl. ast., 16th Jan., 1923; clk. for legal instruments, 26th Feb., 1923.

HOWELL, FREDERICK ROUSE.—B. 1886; sup. clk., P.O., Barbados, Feb., 1907; jun. clk., P.O., Nov., 1907; clk. to master in chancery, Dec., 1907; 4th clk., C.S.O., May, 1909; 3rd clk., C.S.O., 1919; 3rd grade offr., clerk, exec. coun. and exec. comtee., 1925.

HOWELL, JOHN BRUCE, O.B.E. (1927).—B. 1867; 3rd clk., treas., Barbados, July, 1886; 3rd clk., col. sec.'s office, Sept., 1891; 2nd clk., C.S.O.; and clk. of exec. coun. and comtee., Jan., 1898; ag. priv. sec. and A.D.C. to the gov. of Barbados in 1902, 1904, 1906, 1907, 1910 and 1911; J.P., 1918; ch. clk., col. sey., offr., Aug., 1918; ag. col. sec. on various occasions 1922-25; has held various other ag. apptmts.; man. govt. savings bank, 1925.

HOWELL, WILFRED IRVING.—Cadet, botanical and experiment statn., St. Kitts, July, 1907; foreman, Mar., 1909; agri. instr., Nevis, Apr., 1912.

HOWES, ARTHUR BURNABY.—B. 1879; ed. at Dulwich Coll.; called to the bar, Middle Temple, June, 1906; Western circuit; conveyancer, Uganda Prot., May, 1916; custodian of enemy property, Mar., 1917; dist. mag., dist. judge, and admstr.-gen., Entebbe, Uganda, Apr., 1907; dist. mag., dist. judge, and offr. rec. in bankruptcy, Kampala, Uganda, July, 1917; ag. judge of high ct., Jan.-June, 1920; ag. atty.-gen., Feb. to Dec., 1921; senr. mag., Jan., 1922; ag. judge of high ct., Apr. to Oct., 1922 and June, 1923; puisne judge, Gold Coast, Dec., 1924; ag. ch. just., Feb., 1927 and Sept. to Oct., 1928.

HOWITT, CAPT. CHARLES ROBERTS.—B. 1894; ed. Carlisle and Queen's Coll., Oxford; R. Fusiliers, 1914-16; Border Regt., 1916-19; Malayan civ. serv., Nov., 1920; attd. land office, Johore, Dec., 1920; 2nd cls. mag., Sept., 1921; ag. 2nd cls. mag., Johore, May, 1922; 1st cls. mag., May, 1922; passed cadet, June, 1922; asst. collr. of land rev., Johore Bahru, Sept., 1922; offr. cls. V., June, 1922; collr., land rev., Johore Bahru, Oct., 1922; 2nd lieut., J.V.R., Aug., 1923; asst. adviser, Kota Tinggi, May, 1924; lieut., J.V.R., Aug., 1924; attd., pol. cls., Singapore, Oct., 1925; offr. 3rd mag., Singapore, Oct., 1925; offr., cls. IV, June, 1926; dist. offr., Jasir, Dec., 1926.

HOY, SIR WILLIAM WILSON, K.C.B. (1922), KT. BACH. (1916); C.B. (1918).—B. 1868; entd. serv. of Cape Govt. rlyss., 1889; representative of C.G.R. in Johannesburg, 1896; ag. asst. traffic manager, Bulawayo, 1897-8; Kimberley, 1898; asst. traffic manager, Port Elizabeth, 1899; traffic manager, Bloemfontein, Johannesburg, 1900-02; chief traffic manager, C.S.A.R., 1902; represented C.S.A.R. at rly. confee, at Washington; ag. gen. manager in 1905 and 1907; asst. gen. manager, 1909; gen. manager of rlyss. and harbour, Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1910; ret., 1927; chairman., Rhodesia rly. coman., 1927.

HUBBALL, JOHN GORST.—Ck., control and audit office, Cape, 1895; examr., 1895; asst. acctnt., 1903; asst. acctnt., contrlr. and auditor-gen.'s office, Union of S. Africa, 1910; prin. clk., 1912; chief acctnt., treasy., Union of S. Africa, 1916; sec., office of high comsnr. for Union of S. Africa, London, 1928.

HUDDEN, EDWARD LANPHIER.—B. 1902; ed. Radley Coll.; lieut., 4th Battn. Gloucestershire Regiment., T.A., 1925; cadet, Uganda Prot., 1925.

HUDSON, HAROLD.—Book-keeper, treasy. dept., Uganda Prot., Mar., 1911; cashier, treasy. dept., Aug., 1911; asst. treas., Mar., 1914; 1st grade ast. treas., Jan., 1922; ag. deputy treas., June to Dec., 1919, Dec., 1921 to Feb., 1922, Sept., 1922 to Apr., 1923, May, 1923 to Mar., 1924, Feb. to Oct., 1925, Mar. to Dec., 1926, and from Mar. to July, 1927.

HUDSON, PHILIP JAMES.—B. 1897; on mily. serv., Jun., 1916; cadet, Ceylon, Mar., 1920; attd. to Colombo kach., Apr., 1920; pol. mag., Balapitoya, Mar., 1921; asst. settlm. offr., 1922; office ast., Jaffna kach., Dec., 1924; asst. attltm. offr., May, 1925.

HUDSON, LIEUT.-COL. WILLIAM, O.B.E., M.C.—B. 1880; ed. privately and King's Coll., London; S. African War, 1900-02; Queen's Med., with 2 clasps; King's Med., 2 clasps; contr.'s staff, cent. telegrapha, London, 1902; dept., P.M.G., N. Nigeria, 1912; ag. P.M.G., Apr. to Aug., 1912; R.E. (signals), 1914-18; offr. in charge, civ. tels., occupied enemy territory admstrn., Palestine, 1919; P.M.G., Palestine, July, 1920.

HUGGARD, WALTER CLARENCE, K.C., B.A., LL.D.—B. 1884; ed. at Dublin Univ.; 1st honour-man and senr. mod. in legal and polit. science; called to the bar, King's Inns, Dublin, 1907; station mag., Nigeria, Apr., 1914; ag. puisne judge, July to Sept., 1914; pol. mag., Jan., 1917; solr.-gen., Trinidad, Nov., 1920; ag. puisne judge, June-Oct., 1921; K.C., 1921; ag. atty.-gen., Jan.-Oct., 1922; atty.-gen., 1st Nov., 1922; prepared revd. edn., Laws of Trinidad and Tobago, 1925; atty.-gen., Kenya, Feb., 1926; ag. col. sec. and gov.'s dep., Aug., 1927.

HUGGINS, CAPT. JOHN, M.C. (1916).—B. 1891; ed. Bridlington Gram. Schol. and Leeds Univ., B.A.; 2nd lieut., Yorks Regt., Nov.1914; Gallipoli, 1915; Egypt, 1916; France, July lst, 1916; capt., Sept., 1916; ment. in desp.; cadet, F.M.S., 27th Mar., 1920; govt. rice agt., Klang, 28th May, 1920; ag. ast. dist. offr., Kuala Lipis, 7th July, 1920; agt. to food contr., Selangor and Pahang, 7th Oct., 1920; passed exam. in law, Mar., 1921; 4th ast. sec. to govt., 9th Mar., 1921; passed final exam., Malay, June, 1921; dist. offr., Kajang, 24th Aug., 1921; offr., cls. IV., Aug., 1923; recvr., Alsagoff concession, Johore, Feb., 1925; ag. 2nd ast. sec. (A), S.S., Feb., 1926; pvt. sec. to high comsnr., May, 1926; ag. 2nd ast. sec. to govt., F.M.S., Nov., 1927: offr., cls. III, Aug., 1928.
HUGHES, JOHN WHITEHOUSE WARD.—B. 1883; ed. Oakham and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; B.A., 1905; M.A., 1919; cadet, F.M.S., 1906; ag. supt., inland rev., Kelantan, Dec., 1910; mag., Kota Bharu, Sept., 1911; ag. dist. offr., Temerloh, Oct., 1914; ag. aast. adviser, Kelantan, Jan., 1919; ag. collr., land rev., Penang, Oct., 1921; ag. dist. offr., Kuantan, Oct., 1922; ag. Br. adviser, Perlis, June, 1923; offr., cls. I, Dec., 1923; 1st mag., Kuala Lumpur, Apr., 1926; ag. dist. offr., Klang, May, 1927; 1st mag., Kuala Lumpur, June, 1927; ag. comsnr., lands, S.S., Aug., 1927; ag. dist. offr., Klang, May, 1928.

HUGHES, LESLIE DONALD CHARLESTON, M.C.—B. 1890; B.A., Oxon.; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1914; attd. Colombo kach., Dec., 1914; attd. ch., censor's office, Apr., 1915; attd. Badulla kach., Oct., 1915; ag. office asst. to govt. agt., Prov. of Uva, March, 1916; on mil. duty, 1917-19; asst. dir., food prodn., Apr., 1920; pol. mag., Jaffna, Mar., 1921; asst. govt. agt., Batticaloa, Nov., 1921; ag. dist. judge, Badulla, Mar., 1923; asst. sttlmt. offr., Nov., 1923; asst. govt. agt., Maunar, Mar., 1928.

HUGHES, BRIG.-GEN. ROBERT HERBERT WILFRED, C.B. (1921), C.S.I. (1918), C.M.G. (1917), D.S.O. (1916), Officer Legion of Honour (1917)—B. 1872; cadet, H.M.S. "Conway" 1886-87; merchant service, 1887-1898; Bd. of T. master mariner's certif.; sub.-lt., R.N.R., 1896; lieut., 1904; coindr., 1918; capt., 1919; served in S. African war, in S.A. Light Horse, Bethune's M.I., and Royal Navy, from 12th Dec., 1899 to 1st May, 1902; marine offr., S. Nigeria, 27th March, 1903; qualified in surveying at R.G.S. in 1906; elected a younger Brother of Trinity House, 1909; senr. marine offr., 1st Jan., 1909; ag. marine supt. and harbr.-mast., Lagos, 1st July to 10th Dec., 1906; commanded Nigerian govt. yacht "Ivy" as armed auxiliary under the R.N. in the Cameroons Expd., Aug., 1914-Jan., 1916; Trinity House pilot in N. Sea, Apr.-June, 1916; seconded to Army as Major, R.E., 19th June, 1916; lieut.-col., Sept., 1916; brig.-gen., May, 1917; dir. Inland Water Transport, Mespot. till Apr. 1921; demob., 13th Apr. 1921; dir. of marine, Nigeria, Aug., 1921; dir. of marine, Oct., 1921.

HUGHES, RT. HON. WILLIAM MORRIS, P.C. (1916).—B. 1864; M.L.A., New South Wales, 1894-1901; elec. to 1st H. of R., C. of A., 1901, and member since; min. for external affairs 1904; representative of C. of A. at Navigation Conf., London, 1907; atty.-gen., C. of A., Apr., 1910-1913, and from Sept., 1914, to Oct., 1915; prime min., and atty.-gen., 27th Oct., 1916; ditto, 14th Nov., 1916; ditto, 17th Feb., 1917; ditto, 10th Jan., 1918; resigned, Feb., 1923.

HUMPHERSON, LESLIE HERBERT.—B. 1902; ed. King Edward's Schl., Birmingham and Worcester Coll., Oxford; asst. dist. comsnr., Sierra Leone, 7th Jan., 1925.

HUMPHREYS, JOHN LISSETTER, C.M.G. (1928), C.B.E. (1925).—B. 1881; ed. at Bromsgrove Schl. and Brasenose Coll., Oxford (senr. class. scholar, 1900); 1st cls. class. moda., 1902; B.A., 1904; cadet, S. Sttlmts., Oct., 1908; dep. collr. of land rev., and regisr. of deeds, Singapore, May, 1906; ag. dist. offr., Alor Gajah, Malacca, Nov., 1906; passed final exam. in Malay, passed cadet, July, 1907; ag. 3rd mag., Penang, Dec., 1909; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, Mar., 1910; seconded for serv. in Johore as collr. and mag., Batu Pahat, Feb., 1911; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, Nov., 1912; ag. dep. regiar., supr. ct., Singapore, Mar., 1913; also asst. supt. of Indian immigrnt.; seconded for serv. in Johore as asst. advsr., Muar, Feb., 1915; ag. Brit. agt., Trengganu, Nov., 1915; British Adviser, Trengganu, May, 1919; staff, July, 1924 (reed. thanks of S. of S. for services in connection with abolition of debt slavery); ag. Br. adviser, Kedah, May, 1925; gov., Br. N. Borneo, Sept., 1926.

HUMPHRYS, H. L.—Ed. at gram. schl.; Antigua; senior Camb. certif., 3rd div. honours, cashier, treasy., Antigua, Jan., 1892; 2nd indoor offr., 1896; ag. 1st indoor offr. on several occasions; ag. ch. audit clk., Leeward Is., Dec., 1897, to Jan., 1898; ag. audit clk., St. Kitts-Nevis, Dec., 1903, to Mar., 1904; 1st indoor offr. of treasy., Antigua, Apr., 1904; ag. ch. audit clk. and federal acctnt., Leeward Is., May to Oct., 1909, Aug., 1910, and from Apr., 1911 to July, 1912; ag. treaser. of Antigua, and federal treas. from Dec., 1912 to Apr., 1913.

HUNT, ATLEE ARTHUR, C.M.G. (1910).—B. 1864; ed. at Balmain pub. schl. and Sydney; Gram. schl.; entd. lands dept., New S. Wales, 1879; resigned in 1887 to study for the bar; admitted to the bar, 1892, and practised until 1900; priv. sec. to first prime min. of C. of A., Jan., 1901; sec. and permanent head of dept. of external affairs, C. of A., since 1901; attended Imp. Conf., 1907 and 1911; now arbitr., federal pub. service.

HUNT, BERTIE LEONARD.—B. 1883; ed. privately and Queen's Coll., London; trooper, 5th batt. Australian C'wealth Horse, S. African War, 1901-02; Cave Mounted Rifles, 1902-03; B.S.A. Co.'s mounted pol., 1904; various olkships., N. Rhodesia, 1907-10; acctnt., P.W.D., July, 1910; acctnt., London office, B.S.A. Co., May, 1913; seconded to B.S.A. Co.'s comml. branch, N. Rhodesia, 1914-21; acctnt., N. Rhodesia, Sept., 1921; sec. dept. of lands, Apr., 1924.

HUNT, HENRY AMBROSE.—B. 1866; F. R. Met. Soc.; meteorologist, C. of A., 1906.

HUNTER, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR ARCHIBALD, K.C.B. (1898), D.S.O. (1886).—Ed. at Glasgow Acad. and Sandhurst; 4th King's Own Royal Lancaster, 1874; capt., 1882; lieut.-col., 1889; col., 1894; maj.-gen., 1896; served in Egypt, and twice wounded; gov. of Dongola Prov. and commdt. Frontier Field Force, 1895-99; gov. of Omdurman, 1899; Egyptian medal and her orders; in command of 1st cls. dist. in India; lieut.-gen. on staff, commanded 10th div. S.Africa, 1900-01 (twice ment. in desps.); commanded in Scotland, 1901-3; Western Army Corps, India, 1904-7; commanded Southern Army, Indian Army, 1907-9; gov. and comdr.-in-chief, Gibraltar, 1910-1913.

HUNTER, SIR GEORGE, KT. BACH. (1921).—B. 1860; mem., N.Z. parlmt., 1896-99, and since 1911.

HUNTER, HON. GORDON.—B. 1863; ed. Bradford Coll. Inst. and Toronto Univ.; called to the bar, Ontario, 1888; removed to B. Columbia, 1891; ch. just., sup. ct., B. Columbia, 1902.

HUNTER, JAMES BLAKK, B.A. (Univ. of Toronto).—B. 1876; elk., priv. coun. off., Canada, 1899; transfd. to P.O. dept., 1900; marine and fisheries, 1901; pub. wks., 1902 ch. elk., 1907; deputy min. of pub. wks., 1908.

HUNTER, JOHN.—B. 1878; apptd., after compet. exam., elk. of the 2nd div. and assigned to the C.O., Apr., 1899; elk. to patronage comttee., Nov., 1907.
HUNTER, JOHN ADAMS.—B. 1890; ed. at Royal Grammar Sch., Newcastle-on-Tyne and St. John's Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1913 (hist. tripes cls. 2, I.); cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1914; ag. super. visor, cust., Port Dickson, Dec., 1915; ditto, Port Swettenham, Aug.-Dec., 1917; in India studying Tamil, 1918; offr., cls. V, 26th Sept., 1918; asst. dist. offr., Klang, 6th Oct., 1918; addl. to chief sec.'s office, Jan.-Mar., 1919; seconded for serv. in food control dept., 26th Mar., 1919; ag. 3rd asst. sec. to Govt., F.M.S., 7th Oct., 1920; 4th asst. sec. to Govt., 3rd Oct., 1921; offr., cls. IV., offg. dep. contr., lab., Seremban, Nov., 1921; ditto, Kuala Lumpur, July, 1922; on spl. duty, rubber census, July, 1923; offr. in ch., govt. toddy shops in addn., July, 1923; 3rd asst. sec. to govt., F.M.S., Nov., 1923; dist. offr., Ulu Langat, Oct., 1926; offr., Class III, Nov., 1926; ag. sec. to res., Selangor, July, 1927.

HUNTER, K. L.—Asst. dist. commnr., E. Africa Prot., Apr., 1919.

HUNTER, LOUIS LUCIEN.—B. 1889; cadet, local div., Ceylon civ. ser., Sept., 1914; attached to Colombo Kachcheri, Sept., 1914; addl. commnr. of requests and pol. mag., Ratnapura, Oct., 1915; addl. commnr. of requests and pol. mag., Panadura, Sept., 1916; office asst. to govt. agt., N.C. Prov., Aug., 1918; pol. mag., Chilaw, Sept., 1919; addnl. asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Feb., 1922; asst. stimtl. offr., Jan., 1923; addnl. asst. dir., educn., July, 1928.

HURST, RAYMOND GEORGE.—B. 1877; Indian State rly., 1900; E. African rly., 1917; asst. traffic supt., Tanganyika rly., July, 1925.

HUTCHINGS, HUGH H.—Inspr. of govt. schls., Turks and Caicos Is., 1889-1906; J.P., 1901; ch. offr., fire brigade, 1901-19; clk. to commnr. and inspr. of schls., 1907; asst. commnr., Grand Turk, 1908-19; ag. audr., 1908-13; audr., 1913-19; ag. commnr. and ag. judge of sup. ct., five occasions, 1911-19; ag. commnr. of Cayman Is., 1912-13; commnr., Cayman Is., June, 1919.

HUTCHINS, ERNEST ELWIN.—B. 1886; ed. Exeter Schl.; forestry course, Edinburgh Univ., 1903-04; forest dept., S. Africa, 1904; forest demarcat., Kenya, 1909; asst. conservator, forests, Kenya, 1911; E. Africa Mounted Rifles, 1915-16; asst. polit. offr., German E. Africa, 1916-21; admstve. offr., 1st grade, Tanganyika Territory, 1921.

HUTCHINSON, GEORGE STUART MENTETH.—B. 1883; ed. United Services Coll., Westward Ho! and Royal Milv. Coll., Sandhurst; 2nd lieut., unnatd. list, 1902; Indian Army, 1903; capt., 1911; major, 1917; Burma Milv. Pol., Southern Shan States, 1910-14; Indian Expedy. Force, France, 1915; ment. in desps., 1915; invalided, 1917; examining offr., Miny. of Pensions, 1917; regional wounds offr. for Scotland, 1919; apptd. under reconstruction scheme, asst. prin., C.O., 1st Apr., 1924.

HUTCHISON, DONALD MAXWELL WRIGHT, B.Sc. (Eng.), M.I.C.E., A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1882; ed. Wellington Coll. and Faraday House, London; asst. elec. engrnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., 1911; ch. inspr., electy. enact., F.M.S., 1916; dep. ch. engrnr., electy. bd., P.W.D., Jan., 1925; ag. ch. elec. engrnr. and inspr., electy. bd., P.W.D., F.M.S., June, 1926; ch. elec. engrnr. and inspr., electy. dept., F.M.S., Sept., 1926.

HUTSON, SIR EYRE, K.C.M.G. (1922), C.M.G. (1911), B.A.—B. 1864; 2nd clk. to gov. Leeward Is., Oct., 1885; asst. priv. sec. to gov. Barbados, Nov., 1885; priv. sec. to gov. Barbados, Mar., 1887; ditto, at Mauritius, Jan., 1890; at Br. Guiana, July, 1893; Jamaica, 1898; apptd. col. sec. and regir-gen., Bermuda, July, 1901; chrmn., schools comm., 1902; chrmn., St. George's harbour commn., 1903; col. sec. Fiji, July, 1908; chrmn., educn. comm., Apr., 1909; represented Fiji and Western Pacific high comm., at wireless tel. conf., Melbourne, Dec., 1909; dep. gov., May and Oct., 1909, Sept., 1910, Mar., Sept., Oct., 1911, and June, 1912; commnr. of currency, Dec., 1914; ag. gov. of Fiji and high commr. for Western Pacific, Aug., 1915 to May, 1916 and from June to Oct., 1918; gov'r. B. Honduras, 26th Nov., 1918; gov'r., Fiji and high commr., W. Pacific, 1925.

HUTTON, FREDERICK AUGUSTUS.—B. 1862; ed. Bedford Public Schl., S. African Coll. and Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; B.A., 1883; LL.B., 1892; called to the bar, supreme ct., Cape Colony, 1892; prosecutor, special treason ct., 1901-3; judge, supreme ct., assigned to E.D. local divn., 1913; mem., special treason ct., 1915-16; mem. of rebellion enquiry commn., 1916-17; judge, Griqualand West Local Divn., Feb., 1923.

HYAMSON, ALBERT MONTEFIORE, F.R.Hist.S.—B. 1875; ed. Oxford High Schl. and Swansea Gram. Schl.; savings bank dept., G.P.O., London, 1895-98; supplementary estab., sec'y's dept., G.P.O., 1898 to Jan., 1921; dept. of infrn., F.O., Dec., 1917 to Mar., 1918; in charge of sec., miny. of infrn., Apr., 1918 to Nov., 1918; Br. war mission, Nov., 1918 to Mar., 1919; asst. dir., immigrn. and travel, Palestine, Jan., 1921; contrlr. of lab., Dec., 1921; in charge of dept. of immigrn. and travel, Dec., 1923 to Mar., 1924; contrlr. permits, Apr., 1924; sec., cent. town planning commn., Sept., 1922; mem., economy comte., chmn., comte. on rates of wages for govt. employees; dep. chmn., lab. standing comte.; author, "A History of the Jews in England," "Palestine—the Rebirth of an Ancient People," "Palestine, Old and New," "British Projects for the Restoration of the Jews," etc.

IEVERS, C.L., L.R.C.P. (Edin.), L.R.C.S. (Edin.), L.R.F.P.S. (Glas.), D.T.M. (L'pool.).—Apptd. to W.A.M.S., Gold Coast, Feb., 1912; Togoland, 5th to 26th Aug., 1914; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Feb., 1918; senr. med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1921.

IMBERT, A. E.—Labour inspection offr., E. Africa Prot., June, 1919; ch. regir., natives, Kenya, Jan., 1925.

IM THURN, SIR EVERARD F., K.C.M.G. (1905), K.B.E. (1818), C.B. (1900), C.M.G. (1892), M.A.—B. 1802; ed. at Marlborough and Exeter Coll., Oxon; special mag. Pomeroon Dist., Br. Guiana, 1882 to 1890; govt. agt., N.W. dists., 1890; ag. 1st cl. clk., C.O., Dec., 1899; col. sec., Ceylon, 1901; admstd. govt., Ceylon, 1902; gov'r., Fiji, and high commnr., W. Pacific, June, 1904; ret. 1910; rep., Fiji, and W. Pacific at the Coronation of H.M. King George V., 1911; ed. of the Guiana scientific jnl., "Timehri," 1882-7; author of "Among the Indians of Guiana," 1883, and papers on the anthropology, natural history, geography, and history of Guiana; in 1884 made first ascent of Mount Roraima in the interior of Br. Guiana.

INGHAM, RAYWOOD, B.A. (Oxon).—Entered S. Stltmtns. civ. serv., cls. V. (passed in Chinese), Dec., 1912; addl. to monopolies dept., Jan., 1913; dep. collr. of land rev., Malacca, Sept., 1915; pol. mag., Malacca (in addn.), Nov., 1915; collr. war tax, Malacca (in addn.), Mar., 1917; collr., war tax, Singapore (temp.), Mar., 1918; ag. supt. prisons, Malacca (in addn.) Mar.-June, 1919; supernmy. offr., cls. IV., S. Stltmtns., Dec., 1919; asst. prot. Chinese, Singapore, Jan., 1921.
INGLEDOW, Cedric Francis.—B. 1894; on mily. serv., Mar., 1915; cadet, Ceylon, Aug., 1920; attd. to Kurunegala kach., Sept., 1920; ag. office asst. to govt. agt., N.W. Prov., Oct., 1921; ag. pol. mag., Chilaw, Feb., 1922; office asst. to govt. agt., Prov. of Sabaragamuwa, Mar., 1924; ditto to govt. agt., N. Prov., 1926; pol. mag., Matale, Feb., 1926; dist. judge, N’Eliya, Dec., 1927.

INGLES, F. H.—B. 1878; ed. at U.S. Coll., Westward Ho., Newton Coll., Devon, and Jesus Coll., Cambridge; B.A. Cantab., 1902; asst. dist. comntr., S. Nigeria, 6th Oct., 1906; dist. comntr., 2nd grade, 17th Feb., 1913; dist. offr., 1st grade, 20th Oct., 1919; res., 5th Feb., 1922; ag. senr. res., 31st Oct., 1924.

INGRAMS, William Harold.—B. 1897; ed. Shrewsbury; served K.S.L.I., Sept., 1914 to May, 1919; wounded, Belgium, May, 1916; employed, directorate of recruiting, W.O., Dec., 1916; min. of national service, Dec., 1917; min. of lab., demob. and resettlement dept., Nov., 1918; eded. F.Z.S., May, 1919; asst. dist. comntr., Zanzibar, July, 1919; F.R.A.I., 1921; F.R.G.S., 1922; M.R.A.S., 1923; mem., Société d’Anthropologie de Paris, 1923; certif. acad. of internat. law, Hague, 1924; higher standard, Swahili, 1923; ag. dist. comntr., Aug., to Sept., 1923; ag. registr., high ct., offl. assignee and registr., patents, designs and trade marks, Oct., 1923 to Feb., 1924; 2nd asst. sec., Jan., 1925; pvt. sec. to ag. high comntr., Apr. to June, 1925; ditto to Br. req., Nov., 1925 to Aug., 1926 and from Oct. to Nov., 1926; ag. pvt. sec. to H.H. the Sultan, Nov., 1925 to June, 1926; clk., prot. coun., Feb. to June, 1926; edr., Offl. Gaz., in 1924, 1925 and 1927; ag. senr. asst. sec., Mar. to Aug., 1926 and from Oct. 1926 to Feb., 1927; ag. asst. ch. sec., Aug. to Sept., 1926 and Mar. to July, 1927; clk., exec. and leg. couns., Aug. to Oct., 1926 and Mar. to July, 1927; mem. Pemba educn. comttee, and teaching of Koran coman., 1924; mem. museum comttee, 1924 and ag. chmn., Aug., 1926; cls. IV., Order of Brilliant Star, Zanzibar 1927; asst. col. sec., Mauritius, 1927; chmn., museum reorganisation comttee, 1928; chmn., coman. of enquiry, med. and health dept., 1928; part author, “Zanzibar; an account of its People, Industries and History” (1924), “Schl. History of Zanzibar” (1928), and “Aya Za Kuraani” (1928); author “Dialecta of Zanzibar Sultanate” (1924), “Chronology and Genealogies of Zanzibar Rulers” (1926) and various pamphlets and articles.

INMAN, Howard.—B. 1887; B. of T. Certif.; inspr. of weights and measures, G. Coast, 12th June, 1912.

INNES, Cecil Bennett Rose.—Ck., chief acctnt., rlys., 1890; census, 1891; British Bechuanaland serv.; Gordonia, Apr., 1891; relieving ck., Vryburg, Mar., 1892; ck. to P.M.G., Brit. Bechuanaland, May, 1892; sec’s office, Apr., 1893; ck., reger. of deeds, Brit. Bechuanaland, Mar., 1894; deeds office, Vryburg, Sept., 1897; ag. registr., 20th July, 1900; ck. in charge, 1st Dec., 1901; ag. asst. magt., Laingburg, June, 1903; sub-coman., war losses compensation coman., June, 1903; ck. in charge, deeds office, Kimberley, Nov., 1903; rev. ck., civil comntr., Cape, May, 1907; ch. ck., Sept., 1908; receiver of revenue, East London, Dec., 1910; principle ck., recvr. of revenue, Cape Town, Nov., 1916; ch. ck., recvr. of rev., Dec., 1923.

INNES, Rt. Hon., Sir James Rose, P.C. (1915), K.C.M.G. (1901), K.C.—B. 1865; called to the bar of sup. ct., Cape Colony, 12th Feb., 1878; mem. for Victoria East house of assm., Cape, 1884; subsequently reprtd. Cape div.; atty.-gen., 1st Rhodes’ ministry, 17th July, 1890, to May, 1893; selected by Imp. govt. to watch proceedings in connection with trial of reform comttee. prisoners at Pretoria, 1896; atty.-gen. 4th Sprigg ministry, 1900-2; deleg. for Cape Colony to attend comt. in Lond. on final ct. of appeal, 1901; ch. just., sup. ct., Transvaal, 29th Mar., 1902; ordinary judge of appeal, sup. ct., Union of S. Africa, 1910; ch. just. of S. Africa, Oct., 1914; ret., 1st Mar., 1927.

INNESS, William James Deacon, M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.P.H. (Ireland).—B. 1877; ed. Exeter Schl. and St. Mary’s Hosp., Lond.; house physician, Bethelom Royal Hosp.; med. offr., N. Nigeria, 1905; senr. sany. offr., Nigeria, 1914; asst. dir. of med. serv., Nigeria, 1921; dir., med. and sany. services, Sierra Leone, 1924.

INNISS, Knollys Ulric Alexander, M.B., Ch. B. Edin.—B. 1882; entd. med. serv., Trinidad, 16th Aug., 1904; dist. med. offr., 1st Aug., 1912.

INSKIPP, Percy Sidney, O.B.E. (Mily.).—Ck., adminstr.’s off., S. Rhodesia, 1891; ag. sec., 1892; sec. to adminstr., 1893; under sec., 1897; joined London staff, B.S.A. Co., 1900; dir., B.S.A. Co., Apr., 1919; gen. man., B.S.A. Co., S. Africa, June, 1922; mem. of pioneer corps (occupation of Mashonaland), 1890; also served with the Mashonaland horse, Matabele rebellion, 1896 (medal), and Rhodesia field force, 1900 (medal and 2 clasps); joined R.A.S.C., 1914; O.C., R.A.S.C., Harwich dist., 1914-17; S.S.O., 48th divn., France, Flanders, Italy, 1917-19; Croce di Guerra, Italy; ment. in desps.

IRBY, G. N.—B. 1889; ed. Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford; 2nd lieut., Oxford and Bucks. L.I., May, 1915; invalided with rank of capt., Jan., 1918; asst. priv. sec. (apptmts.) to Lord Milner, July, 1920; to Mr. Churchill, Feb., 1921; the Duke of Devonshire, Oct., 1922; Mr. J. H. Thomas, Jan., 1924; Mr. L. C. M. S. Amery, Nov., 1924.

IRELAND, Frederick Joseph.—B. 1903; apptd., after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 30th Sept., 1920.

IRVINE, Frederick Robert, M.Sc. Ag., Fellow, Linnean Soc. (1927).—B. 1898; ed. Royal Grammar Sch., Newcastle-on-Tyne; war serv., Gordon Highlanders, France and Belgium, 1916-19; 2nd lieut., R.A.F., 1918, R.Sc., agr., Armstrong Coll., Durham Univ., 1920; teacher of agr. and biology, Achimota, Gold Coast, 1924.

IRVINE, Robert, M.C. (1917), Croix de Guerre (1918).—B. 1894; ed. Dunfermline; capt., Lancs. Fusiliers, 1918; cadet, F.M.S., 15th Oct., 1919; 3rd asst. sec., Fed. sect., May, 1920; 4th asst. sec. to govt., F.M.S., July, 1920; passed final exam., Malay and law, Feb., 1920; priv. sec. to ch. sec., F.M.S., Mar., 1921; asst. dist. offr., Tanpin, Apr., 1922; offr., clu. V., Nov., 1922; 2nd lieut., M.V.I., Mar., 1923; ag. 2nd mag., Kuala Lumpur, May, 1923; dist. offr., Jelebu, Nov., 1924; asst. dist. offr., Lower Perak, Jan., 1925; offr., cls. IV., July, 1925; ag. 2nd asst. sec. (A), S.S., May, 1926 and Feb., 1928; ag. 1st asst. sec. (B), S.S., Feb., 1928; ditto and clk. of course., Mar., 1928.
IRVINE, Hon. Sir Wm. Hill, K.C.M.G. (1914), LL.D., K.C.—B. 1868; called to the bar, Victoria, 1884; premier of Victoria, 1902-4; mem. H. of R., C. of A., since 1906; atty.-gen., C. of A., June, 1913 to Sept. 1914; chief just., Victoria, 5th Apr., 1918; lieut.-gov., Victoria, 11th May, 1918.

IRVING, Francis Ernest.—B. 1886; ed. at St. Andrew's Coll. and Marist Bros. Schl., S. Africa; served in Boer War, 1901-2; German S.W. Africa, with Imp. Light Horse, 1914-15; German E. Africa, 1916; seconded to admstn. of Mafia Is., as finan. offr., Nov., 1916, to May, 1919; asst. cust. dept., Zanzibar, Oct., 1919; ag. asst. ch. of cust. for various periods, 1920-22; asst. ch. of cust., 17th Dec., 1922; ag. ch. of cust., 31st Mar., 1924 to 18th Mar., 1925 and various periods since.

IRVING, Henry Edward, M.B.E. (1918).—Ed. at Charterhouse and Handelshausanstalt, Leipzig; trooper, 9th Lancers, 1899-1902; served in S. African campaign; ch. clk. to central repatriation bd., O.R.C., Mar., 1902; clk. to col. sec., Oct., 1902; clk. to adminstr., O.F.S. Prov., 10th Aug., 1910; ch. clk. to prov. sec. (2nd grade), 16th Oct., 1924.

IRVING, Hugh Crauford.—Asst. dist. commnr., Somaliland Prov., June, 1914.

IRWIN, 1st Baron (cr. 1925), Hon. Edward Frederic Lindley Wood.—B. 1881; ed. Eton and Christ Church and All Souls, Oxford (M.A. and fellow); major, Yorkshire Dragoons; M.P., Ripon divn., Yorks, 1910-25; under sec. of state for the cols., Apr., 1921; min. of educn., Oct., 1922; viceroy of India, 1926.

IRWIN, Henry Mark, B.A.—B. 1885; ed. Haileybury and Selwyn Coll.; Cambridge exhibtioner; Haileybury exhibitioner; hona. class. tripos, 1908; asst. rea., N. Nigeria, 1908; attached to secretariat, July to Dec., 1911; priv. sec. to ag. gov., C. L. Temple, Esq., C.M.G., June, 1912.

IRWIN, Robert Edward.—B. 1899; ed. at Christ's Hosp.; col. audlt. dept., Oct., 1925; asst. audtr., Tanganyika Territory, Nov., 1925.

ISAACS, Rt. Hon. Sir Isaac Alfred, P.C. (1921), K.C.M.G. (1928).—B. 1855; called to the bar, Victoria, 1880; Q.C., 1899; M.L.A., Victoria, 1892-1901; solr.-gen., 1893; atty.-gen., 1894-9; and again in 1900; mem. of Aust. Fed. Convention, 1897-8; and of first Federal parlmt.; atty.-gen. in Deakin ministry, 1905-6; judge of High Ct. of Australia, Oct., 1906; ag. ch. just., 1925 and 1927.

ISAACS, Frank Noel.—B. 1871; Jamaica civ. serv., 1890; held appts. in various depts., 1891-1907; clk. of wks. and acctnt., new pub. bldgs., 1909; sec., bd. of supervision, 1910; sec., malaria comm., 1910-12; exec. offr., malaria comm., 1910-12; drought and hurricane relief offr., 1912-17; ag. prot., immigrts., 1914; man., Rio Cobre home, 1917; commnr., parish of St. Catharine, 1921; sec., child welfare comm., 1921.

ISHERWOOD, Albert Arthur Mangnall, O.B.E. (1926), M.A. (Oxon).—B. 1889; ed. St. John's schl., Leatherhead, and University Coll., Oxford; jur. supt., educn. dept., N. Nigeria, 9th July, 1913; loaned to polit. dept., N. Nigeria, 1915-17; polit. offr., Tanganyika adminstr., 8th Oct., 1917; ag. senr. commnr., Feb., 1923 to Jan., 1924; dep. dir., educn., Sept., 1924; ag. dir., educn., Oct., 1924 to Mar., 1925; ditt. and mem., exec. comm., Mar. to Nov., 1927; Swahili examr.

ISLINGTON, 1st Baron (cr. 1910), Rt. Hon. Sir John Poynier Dickson-Poynier, G.C.M.G. (1911); D.S.O. (1900); J.P.—B. 1866; ed. at Harrow and Christ Church, Oxford; major and hon. col., Wilts Yeomanry; served in S. Africa, 1900 (Queen's medal, 3 clasps); late lieut., 3rd Royal Scots; mem. L.C.C., 1898-1904; M.P., Chippenham, Wilts, 1892-1910; gov., New Zealand, 1910-1912; chmn. of Indian civ. ser. comm., 1912; parly. under sec. of state for the colonies, 1914; parly. under sec. for India, 1915.

IVES, William Carlos, B.C.L.—B. 1873; ed. pub. schl., Pincher Creek, Alta., Coaticook, Queb., and McGill Univ.; puisne judge, sup. ct., Alta., 1914.

IZARD, H.—Asst. dist. commnr., E. Africa Prot., Feb., 1915.

JACKLIN, S., M.C.—Acctnt., repat. dept., Christiana, Aug., 1902; rev. clk., law dept., Nov., 1902; clk., civ. commn. off., Pretoria, Nov., 1903; clk., rev. dept., Mar., 1905; prin. clk., Oct., 1906; prin. clk., inland rev. dept., Apr., 1912; inspr., inland rev. dept., Nov., 1916; survr., inland rev. dept., Apr., 1918; ag. dep. commnr., Johannesburg, Sept., 1919; ch. clk., estabmtns., treasy., Union of S. Africa, 1st Jan., 1920; sec., pub. ser. commn., Oct., 1921; ret., 18th Oct., 1926; treas., League of Nations, 18th Oct., 1926.

JACKMAN, Edward Clarence.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; ent. Middle Temple, 1889; lecture prizeman, real property, 1890; lecture prizeman, equity, 1891; called to bar, 1892; practised at Barbados bar; elec. to H. of A., Barbados, 1904-1913; mem., exec. comttee., 1909-1913; pol. mag., Bridgetown, Barbados, 1913; asst. judge, ct. of appeal, Barbados, 1921.

JACKS, Philip—B. 1877; ed. Plymouth Coll.; admtd. solr., sup. ct., England, 1900; asst. land offr., Hong Kong, 1900; J.P., 1906; commnr. for oaths, 1906; ag. land offr., 1907 to 1908; ag. land offr. and offr. recvr. in bankruptcy, 1908; ag. land offr., 1911; and from 1913-1914; land offr., 1916; ag. crown solr., 1919 and 1920; called to the bar (Inner Temple), 1922; ag. puisne judge, 1927-28.

JACKSON, Edward St. John, O.B.E. (1918).—Ed. Stonyhurst and Beaumont Colleges and Brazenose College, Oxford; B.A., 1908; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1910; legal advisor, Gambia, 26th Oct., 1912; atty.-gen., Nyasaland, Oct., 1918; judge of high ct., July, 1920; pres. of lands commnr., 1920; pres., finance commn., 1923; atty.-gen., Tanganyika Territory, 20th Aug., 1924.

JACKSON, Major Francis Walter Fitton, C.M.G. (1928), D.S.O. (1917).—B. 1881; ed. Dover Coll.; entd. B.A., 1899; served in S. Africa, 1901-2; seconded to W.A.F.F., 30th July, 1904; dist. commnr., Northern Territories, G. Coast, 1st Jan., 1907; asst. col. sec., G. Coast, 10th Mar., 1911; provincial commnr., G. Coast, 23rd Jan., 1915; services lent to W.O., Mar., 1915, to Apr., 1919; served in France, May, 1915, to June, 1918; ment. in desps. 3 times; O.C.: British forces, and senr. polit. offr., Togoland, July, 1919; represented gov't., in final handing over of Lome and that portion of Togoland ceded to France by the Franco-British declrn. of 10th July, 1919; dep. ch. commnr., Ashanti, 1928.

JACKSON, Sir Frederick John.—K.C.M.G. (1913); C.B. (1899); C.M.G. (1902); ed. at Shrewsbury Schl. and Jesus Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. asst., Uganda Prot., July, 1894; vice-consul, May, 1895; dep. commnr., Apr., 1901; dep.
JAMES, Sir Frederick Seton, K.B.E. (1922), C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1870; ed. at Charterhouse and abroad; asst. dist. commr., Niger Coast Prot., 1896; in charge at Opobo and Akwete, 1896-7; with peaceful mission to Bende in 1897; trav. commr., 1897; serv. as polit. offr. in expedit. agat. Ekuris, Cross River, 1898; settled disputes in Qua country after cent. div. exped., 1899; read. thanks of S. of S. divanl. commr., 1901; intell. and polit. offr. with Aro field force, 1901-2 (desp. medal); read. thanks of dir.-gen. of intell. and S. of S. in connection with map of Aro operations; ag. sec. and dep. high commr., 1905; with Kwale patrol, Nov., 1906 (clasp); prov. commr. and mem. of exec. and legis. couns. of S. Nigeria on amalgamation, 1906; ag. col. sec. from 29th Mar., 1907; dep. gov., Apr. and Sept., 1907; ag. col. sec., and deputy gov. on various occasions from 1908 to 1912; ag. gov., Feb. to Sept., 1912; apptd. admnstr. on amalgamation of N. and S. Nigeria, 1st Jan., 1914; col. sec., Straits Settlements, June, 1916; seconded for spl. services as food contr., S. Stilmtz. and Malay States, Dec., 1918; O.A.G. S. Stilmtz. and high commr., Malay States, Aug., 1919; col. sec. in addition, May, 1919; O.A.G., Apr., 1922; col. sec., Feb., 1920; ag. ch. sec., F.M.S., June-Oct., 1920; col. sec., May, 1921; gov., Windward Is., 23rd Feb., 1924; assumed gov., 26th July, 1924.

JAMES, Godfrey Warden.—B. 1888; ed. at St. Paul's schl., London (Junior and Senior Foundation Scholar) and Oriol Coll., Oxford (Cornwallis Exhibt., 1906), hons. in class. meda., 1909, and lit. hum., 1911; B.A. 1920; M.A., 1924; called to the bar, Middle Temple, Apr., 1923; asst. dist. commr., Sierra Leone, Jan., 1914; has acted as dist. commr., Port Loko sub-dist., Bombail sub-dist., and Sherbro dist., and as asst. col. sec., for various periods from 1914-19; dist. commr., May, 1920; dist. commr., headqrs. dist., Mar., 1922.

JAMES, Herbert Basil.—Ed. Jesus Coll., Oxford (exhibitioner), 2nd class math. mods., 1908; 3rd class final honour schl. nat. science, 1910; asst. res., Northern Nigeria, 30th Nov., 1910.

JAMES, Joseph Edward.—B. 1867; ed. at pub. schls. and Mico Coll., Antigua; ag. educn. offr., Antigua, Nov., 1901; olk., educn. dept. and educn. offr., Antigua, Apr., 1904; schlmast., St. John's Training Schl., Antigua, Feb., 1913, to June, 1917; sub-inspr.schls., Antigua, 1st Apr., 1914; sub-inspr., schl., St. Kitts-Nevis, 1919; local inspr., schl., Mar., 1927; ag. fedl. inspr., schl., July, 1928.

JAMES, Marshall Nicol.—B. 1875; served under the condominium govt., New Hebrides until Mar., 1922; govt. agt., New Hebrides, Mar., 1922.

JAMES, Sir Walter Hartwell, Kt. B.A.C. (1907).—Ed. in Perth at state and high schls., admitted as barrister and solicitor, 1888; member for East Perth, 1894; represented W. Aust. at fed. conven., 1897-8; hon. minister, 1901; K.C., 1902; premier and atty.-gen., 1902; agt.-gen. for W.A., 1904-1906.

Jamison, Robert, M.B., B.Ch., B.A.O. (Ireland), F.R.C.S. (Eng.), D.T.M. (Lond.).—B. 1880; asst. med. offr., Hiatiikulu, Swaziland, 1910-13; med. offr., Swaziland, 1913; served, S.W. Africa campaign, 1914-15; prin. med. offr., 1918.
JANSEN, HON. ERNEST GEORGE, B.A., LL.B., M.L.A.—B. 1881; ed. Ladysmith Govt. Schl. and Durban High Schl.; leader of Nationalist party in Natal; mem., Natal Univ. Coll. Coun.; chmn., Saamwerk Unie van Natale Vereeniginge (the first body in S.A. to prescribe exams. in Afrikaans) for 7 years; rep. Vryheid in parl. since 1921; foundation mem. of Suid Afrikaanse Akademie vir Taal, lettere en kuns; elec. speaker, Union H. of A., 26th July, 1924.

JANSEN, FRANCOIS JOHANNES.—B. 1869; ed. Graaff Reinet Coll.; mag.'s clk., Fraserburg, Feb., 1889; Beaconfield, Jan., 1890; examr. of accts., C.O., Oct., 1892; civ. comsmr.'s clk. and ast. mag., Barkly West, Dec., 1894; Aliwal North, May, 1895; Dordrecht, July, 1895; gh. clk. and paymr., Cape pol., Kimberley, Nov., 1897; ast. plague admstr., Apr., 1901; ast. guardians fund, Mar., 1902; sub-commr., war losses compensation comsmr., Aug., 1902; regiar., sup. ct., Eastern dists., Apr., 1904; civ. comsmr. and res. mag., Murraysburg, Oct., 1907; Victoria West, Dec., 1910; gh. clk., dept. of just., Sept., 1917; civ. comsmr., and mag., Uitenhage, Feb., 1923; East London, Feb., 1924.

JANSZ, HERBERT ERIC.—B. 1890; cadet, local division, Ceylon civ. ser., Sept., 1914; attached to Kandy kach., Sept., 1914; attached to Batticaloa kach., Dec., 1914; addtl. pol. mag., Batticaloa, in addition, Aug., 1915; ag. office ast. to gov't. ast., Batticaloa, Sept., 1915; office ast. to ast. gov't. ast., Regalla, Jan., 1917; office ast. to gov't. ast., N. Prov., Jan., 1918; pol. mag., Kalutara, Mar., 1920; dist. judge, Ratnapura, Jan., 1923; addnl. dist. judge, Avissawella, in addn., Oct., 1927; ast. stlitm. offr., Sept., 1928.

JANSZ, JONATHAN CHARLES.—B. 1871; ols. V., Ceylon civ. serv., Sept., 1928; extra office ast., Galle kach., Sept., 1928.

JARDINE, DOUGLAS JAMES, O.B.E. (1918),—B. 1888; ed. at Westminster and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; 2nd cls. classical trip., 1910; B.A., 1910; M.A., 1914; chief sec.'s off., Cyprus, 1910; pvt. sec. to ag. high comsmr., July to Oct., 1911; ast. sec. to gov't., 1912; ag. ch. ast. sec. on several occasions, 1912-16; passed in modern Greek, 1912; sec. to the admstr., Somaliland, 1916; accompanied mission to Abyssinia on occasion of coronation of the Empress Zauditu (3rd cls. Star of Ethiopia), 1917; in charge H.Q. services, Somaliland Expedy. Force, 1920 (A.G.S. med. and ment. in desp.); senr. ast. sec., Nigerian secretariat, 1921; ag. dep. ch. sec., July to Nov., 1926 and June to Aug., 1926; dep. ch. sec., Tanganyika Territory, May, 1927; ag. ch. sec., June to Nov., 1927 and Apr. to Oct., 1928; gov't. dep. on several occasions, 1927-28; ch. sec., Jan., 1929; joint-editor "Handbook of Cyprus," 1913 and 1919, and author of "Mad Mullah of Somaliland," 1923.

JARDINE, GORDON MURRAY.—Ed. Marlborough Coll. and Clare Coll., Camb.; ast. dist. comsmr., Uganda, 1912; cov. commdr., 4th Batt. K.A.R., 1917-18; called to the bar (Inner Temple), 1919; dist. mag., Tanganyika Territory, 1919; ret. without taking up appl., 1920; dist. mag., Entebbe, Uganda, 1921.

JARRETT, NORMAN ROWSTONE.—B. 1889; ed. Highgate and Exeter Coll., Oxford, 3rd cls. class. mods., 1910, 2nd cls. lit. hum., 1912; B.A., 1912; cadet, F.M.S., 1912; passed final exam. in Tamil, Apr., 1914; ag. ast. contrlr. of lab., Apr., 1914; passed exam. in law, July, 1914; ag. ast. dist. offr., Klang, Apr., 1915; ag. dist. offr., Klang, in addn., Nov., 1917; ag. dist. offr., K. Selangor, Aug., 1919; ast. dist. offr., Klang, Sept., 1920; dist. offr., Kuala Langat, Mar., 1921; ag. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, Apr., 1925; ag. ast. adviser, Kelantan, Dec., 1926.

JARVIS, CYRIL CHESTER.—B. 1884; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; Rhodes schol., 1904; Wadham Coll., Oxford, B.A. (hon. juris.); LL.B., Cape Univ.; sec., ch. just., Cape Colony, 1907; admitted Cape bar, 1910; ch. clk. to atty.-gen., O.F.S.; prof. ast. to atty.-gen., Cape Prov., 1921; crown pros., Johannesburg, 1926.

JAYARATNE, MEERENNA FRANCIS DE SILVA, B.A. (Lond.).—B. 1904; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Feb., 1927; addl. Colombo kach., Mar., 1927; office ast., Matale kach., Jan., 1928.

JEBB, R. R. H., O.B.E. (1918).—B.A. (Oxon.), B. 1882; ast. auditor, S. Leone, Jan., 1907; ast. auditor, E.A.P., Nov., 1909; ast. dist. comsmr., Somaliland Prot., 1915; dist. comsmr., 1913.

JEFF, CAPT. JOHN.—B. 1896; cadet, F.M.S., addl. Chinese prot., Ipoh, Apr., 1920; ag. ast. prot., Chinese, Selangor, Jan., 1923; ast. prot., Chinese, Seremban, Dec., 1923; addl. cust. dept., Jan. 1925; ag. ast. dir., educn. (Chinese), Nov., 1926; offr., cls. IV., Apr., 1927; ag. ast. dir., educn., schla. (Chinese), S.S. and F.M.S. in addn., Oct. to Nov., 1927; ag. prot., Chinese, Perak, Apr., 1928.

JEFFERY, GEORGE, O.B.E. (1924), F.S.A.—Scholarship, R. Coll. of Art and Science, 1872; scholarship in architecture, R. Academy of London (1874); F.R.I.B.A., 1892; architect to Rt. Rev. Bishop in Jerusalem and the East, 1892; hon. corre. mem. of Imperial Institute of Archaeology of Russia, 1897; local sec. for Cyprus Society of Antiquaries; inspr. of pub. wks., Cyprus, 1898; curator of ancient monuments, Cyprus, 1903; relinquished appt. July, 1919; reapptd. curator of ancient monuments, Cyprus, Feb., 1921; author of "Summary of Architectural Monuments of Cyprus," "Cyprus under an English King," "Historic Monuments of Cyprus" and of several papers on the medieval archaeology of Cyprus and Jerusalem.

JEFFRIES, CHARLES J., O.B.E. (1928).—B. 1896; ed. Malvern Coll.; class demy., Magdalen Coll., Oxford, 1914; 2nd lieut., 3rd Wilshire Regt., Sept., 1915; served in France, 1916; lieut., 1917; invalided from army, Nov., 1917; tempy. 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 27th Dec., 1917; apptd., under reconstruction scheme, 2nd cls. clk., 16th July, 1919; sec., E. Africa land stlitm. selection board, 1919; ast. sec., E. Africa currency board; prin., 1st Apr., 1920; hon. sec., Coroma Club, since 1921; sec., comte., on governors' pensions, 1927-28.

JEFFRIES, CHARLES WILLIAM, F.R.A.S.—B. 1882; Computer, Royal Observatory, Greenwich, 1897; junr. ast., Royal Observatory, Cape of Good Hope, 1902; 1st ast., Royal Observatory, Hong Kong, 1907; chief ast., ditto, 1912; ag. dir. in 1915, 1920, 1924 and 1925.

JEKYLL, LIEUT.-COL. SIR HERBERT K.C.M.G. (1901), R.E., C.M.G. (1885).—B. 1846; lieut. R.E., Apr., 1866; employed under War Office and Trinity House in 1868 to 1870, and destruction of sunken ships, from submarine mining, and under G.P.O. in the telegraph dept., from 1870 to 1873, and 1874 to 1876; served in the campaign of 1873-74 on the G. Coast; priv. sec. to the Earl of Carnarvon Jan., 1877, to Feb., 1878; sec. to the col. defence comte., 1878; sec. to the roy. comm.
on the defence of Br. possessions and commerce abroad, 1879-82; specially employed to visit and report on the defences of Singapore and Colombo, 1883-4; sec. col. defence comtee., 1885; priv. sec. to Lord Carnarvon, viceroy of Ireland, June, 1886, to Jan., 1886; sec. to roy. comsn. for Melbourne centennial exhib., 1888; priv. sec. to lord-lieut. of Ireland, 1892-5; sec. to the roy. comsn. for the Paris exhibition, 1900.

JELF, ARTHUR SELBORNE, C.M.G. (1927).—B. 1876; ed. Marlborough and Exeter Coll., Oxford (exhr.); 2nd cls. class. mods., 1897; 3rd cls. lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; M.A., 1913; cadet, F.M.S. civ. serv., 1899; held various admstve. and exec. posts in Malay States, 1900-10; ast. gen. adviser to Johore govt., Jan., 1911; offr. of cls. IV., Jan., 1912; chmn., san. bd., Kinta, Perak, Apr., 1914 to Apr., 1917; 2nd lieut., M.S.V.R., 16th Sep., 1914; lieut., M.S.V.R., Jan., 1915; seconded for mil. serv. (lieut. general list), Apr., 1917; offr. of cls. III., Dec., 1917; tempy. capt., gen. staff, S. Stilts command; attchd. gen. staff, W.O. (milit. intell.), Jan., 1918; H.M. Petroleum Exec. (sec. to Lord Harcourt's comtee.), June, 1918; offr., cls. II., 1st June, 1919; ag. dist. offr., Larut, Perak, Nov., 1919; ag. under sec. to govt., F.M.S., June, 1920; dir., Malayan polit. intell. bureau, cls. Ia, Dec., 1923; ag. contr. lab., S.S. and F.M.S., Mar., 1924; pres., estates health comsn., Apr., 1924 (reed. thanks of S. of S.); col. sec., Jamaica, Oct., 1925; ag. gov., Oct., 1925 to Apr., 1926; and June to Nov., 1928; lieut.-col., local forces, Oct., 1927.

JELLIICOE, 1ST VISCOUNT OF SOAPA (CREAT. 1918).—Sir JOHN RUSHWORTH JELLIICOE, O.M. (1916), G.C.B. (1915), G.C.V.O. (1916).—B. 1859; entd. navy, 1872; served in Egyptian war, 1882; China expeditionary force, 1900; European war, 1914-16; battle of Jutland; naval ast. to controller, 1901-3; dir. of naval ordnance, 1905-7; A.D.C. to King Edward VII., 1906-7; 3rd sea lord of the Admiralty and controller of the navy, 1908-10; comdr.-in-chief of the Atlantic fleet, 1910-11, and of the Grand Fleet, 1914-16; 2nd sea lord of the Admiralty, 1912-14; 1st sea lord, 1916-17; admiral of the fleet, 1919; governor-general of New Zealand, 1920-1924; G.C. Legion of Honour, and Croix de Guerre (France); G.C. Order of Leopold, and Croix de Guerre (Belgium); St. George 3 (Russia); G.C.R.S. with Pavlovna (Japan); G.C. Savoia (Italy).

JENKINS, GEORGE FREDERICK.—Min. of agr. and asst. min. of repatriation, S. Australia, 3rd Nov., 1922.

JENKINS, REGINALD FREDERICK.—B. 1901; entered C.O., 30th Nov., 1916; apptd., after compet. exam., ast. clk., C.O., Oct., 1918; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; seconded to Empire Marketing bds., 1926; cler. offr., higher grade, 1st Feb., 1928.

JENKINS, SIDNEY THOMAS.—B. 1883; ed. St. Gabriel's, Bristol; large and small scale draughtsman, cadastral and topographical surv.; surv. draughtsman, Zanzibar, 1926.

JENKS, J. C. A.—Ed. Bristol Gram. Schl. and Angers, France; awarded Croix-de-Guerre (Palm) 1917; Order of Saint Stanislaus with Swords (2nd cls.), and med. in desps., 1919; colonial audit serv., 1920; ast. audr., Kenya Colony, Apr., 1920; ast. audr. in charge, Zanzibar, Mar., 1923; senr. ast. audr. in charge, Jan., 1926; mem., retrenchment and rev. comtee., Zanzibar, 1927.

JENNER, FRANK.—B. 1878; served in Cape Mounted Rifles, Bechuana land campaign, 1896-97; S. African war, 1899-1901; sub-instr., Basuto land Mounted Pol., 1901; instr., 1910; supt., leper stlitnt., 1914; comnr., 1920.

JENNINGS, F. G.—Ast. dist. comnr., E.A.P., Apr., 1919.

JENYNS, ROGER SOANE.—B. 1904; ed. Eton and Magdalene Coll., Cambridge; cadet Hong Kong, 31st Dec., 1926.

JEPSON, ALWYN HALL.—B. 1878; ed. Mechanics Inst., Hyde; imperial postal telegraph service, 1893; S. African War, 1900-2 (medal and 5 bars); military telegraphs, Ceylon, 1903-6; acted as supt., military telegraphs, and instr. in telegraphy and telephony, Colombo; ag. overseer, Manchester, 1907; postmaster, Nyasaland, 1907; supt., telephones, 1911; offr.-in-charge posts and telegraphs, Nyasaland Field Force, 1914-17 (1914 Star, etc.); lieut., 1915; ast. postmaster-gen., 1915; ag. postmaster-gen., Apr. to June, 1917, Apr. to Dec., 1919 and from Mar., 1922 to Feb., 1923; postmr. gen., Feb., 1923.

JEPSON, FRANK PRICE.—B. 1885; M.A. Pembroke Coll., Camb.; exhib., medallist, and dip. in agri. (hons. in entomology), Wye Agric. Coll., Kent, 1906; trop. disease research fund student in med. entomology, Camb. Univ., 1907; assisted in investig. by L.G.B. on flies as carriers of infection, 1908 and 1909; govt. entomologist, Fiji, 1909; offr. visits to Hawaii, 1911, Samoa, 1912, Java, 1913; ast. entomologist, Ceylon, 1919; ag. entomologist in adnin., July, 1923 to Mar., 1924 and Oct. to Nov., 1925; del. to Imp. Ag. Research Confe., Lond., 1927; on sp. serv., U.S.A. (termite investig.), 1928.

JERRAM, JAMES HAVELOCK.—B. 1879; ed. Thames High Schl. and Auckland Gram. Schl., N.Z.; ent. N.Z. state fire insurance office, 1905; acct., 1906; dep. gen. man., 1908; gen. man., 1921.

JEROVSE, RICHARD SOMERVILLE.—B. 1887; ed. Bradfield Coll. and Magdalen Coll., Oxford (hist. demy); cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1911; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, Mar., 1913; ag. ast. sec. to res., Perak, July, 1913; ag. 2nd ast. dist. offr., Kuala Kangsar, Aug., 1913; ag. ast. dist. offr., Bruas, Oct., 1914; ast. dist. offr., Lower Perak, Jan., 1920; dist. offr., Pasir Putih, July, 1920; ag. judge, high ct., Kelantan, 1921; dist. offr., Tampin, June, 1922; chmn., sany. bd., Larut, Jan., 1924; ag. dist. offr., Upper Perak, Apr., 1924; chmn., sany. bd., Larut, Oct., 1924; 1st mag. and regt., sup. ct., Johore Bharu, Oct., 1924; ag. ast. audr.-gen., F.M.S., May, 1925; ch. ast. dist. offr., Kinta, Aug., 1925; dist. offr., Krian, joint examr., Malay, Perak, Oct., 1927; ag. mag., Kuala Lumpur, Mar., 1928.

JEWELL, M.—B. 1880; Apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., Apr., 1899, conf. clk., 1911; deptl. ast., 1st Apr., 1922.

JEWELL, NORMAN PARSONS, O.B.E. (1929)—M.C. (1917); M.D.; B.Ch.; B.A.O., Trin. Coll., Dub.; L.M., Rotunda, Dub.; B.A. (Moderator), Trin. Coll., Dub.; late anaesthetist, Dun's Hosp., Dub.; ast. med. offr., Seychelles, 1910; J.P.; ast. and chmn. local bds. of health, Praslin and La Digue; med. supt., leper asylum; med. offr., R.A.P., 1915; senr. med. offr., Kenya, Feb., 1921; ag. surg. specialist, European hosp., Nairobi, 1926.

JOHNS, FRN., F.J.I.—B. 1868; ed. Cornwall, England; on Adelaide newspaper literary staffs from 1885 to 1914; leader of the first offl. Hansard staff, S. Australian parl., since July, 1914; author of "John's Notable Australians"
(1906 and 1908), and of "Australasia's Prominent People," "Notables, Past and Present" ("Who's Who in Australia" (seven editions), and "A Journalist's Jottings"; sec. of Adelaide branch of Royal Society of St. George, and hon. sec., Matthew Flinders' National Statue, City of Adelaide; also hon. sec., Princess Mary wedding gift fund, S. Australia.

JOHNSON, D. O.—B. 1873; entd. Bahamas civ. ser., 1904; Out Island commr. (3rd div.), 1909; 2nd div., 1910; 1st div., 1914.

JOHNSON, R. T.—Res. mag., E. Africa Prot., 1915; senr. res. mag., Kenya, Dec., 1922; ag. judge, 1924 and 1925.

JOHNSON, ELLEN M.—B. 1873; ast. clk., post office, 11th Sept., 1914; ch. clk., 1st Jan., 1924; ag. postmtr., 16th May to 31st Oct., 1925; ast. postmtr., 26th June, 1926.

JOHNSON, FREDERICK ENGLAND, A.F.I.A. (Australia).—B. 1878; served in S. African war, 1899–1901 (Queen's medal, 3 clasps); inspr. of native labourers, British residency, New Hebrides, 1909; in charge of scots. of British residency, 1909; ag. comdt. of British div. of native constab., 1908, 1910, 1912, and from 1914, in addition to other duties; is also a dep. commr. of the high commr.'s ct. for the W. Pacific, and ag. registr. of high commr.'s ct., in the New Hebrides; treas., and collr. of cust., Br. Solomon Is., 25th Nov., 1909.

JOHNSON, CAPT. GEORGE BENJAMIN.—B. 1884; ed. Ryder's Schl., Devonport and Cheltenham Training Coll. (dipl. educum.); Leicester Regt. and gen. staff, 1915–19; res. of offrs., T.A.; ag. vice-consul, Le Havre, 1920; headmnr., Zanzibar educn. dept., 1920; ditto and inspr., schls., 1925; ag. dir., educn. in 1920–23, 1925–26 and 1928; ch. inspr. schls., 1928.

JOHNSON, GEORGE CUNYNGHAM.—B. 1875; 2nd clk., treas., St. Kitts, Apr., 1894; 2nd clk. admstr.'s office and clk. of legis. coun., Mar., 1896; clk. to admstr. and clk. of couns., Jan., 1901; treas. and comptlr., cust., St. Kitts-Nevis, June, 1923; ag. admstr., St. Kitts-Nevis, June, 1923; offl. mem., exec. and legis. couns., St. Kitts-Nevis, and offl. mem., Fed. exec. coun., censor, St. Kitts during the war; is a J.P. for St. Kitts-Nevis; ag. col. sec., Leeward Is. and admstr. govt., Antigua, June, 1925; ag. commr., Montserrat, Feb., 1927.

JOHNSON, JOHN COLEMAN DE GRAFT.—B. 1884; ed. Wesleyan Coll. Schl., Cape Coast; 5th grade clk., Ashanti, 1907; 4th grade clk., police dept., 1912; ast. inspr. W. and M., 1914; ast. sec. for nativ. affrs., 23rd Mar., 1920; mem., Accra town coun., Jan., 1928.

JOHNSON, HON. SIR WILLIAM ELLIOT, K.C.M.G. (1920).—B. 1862; speaker of the H. of R., C.of.A., 1913–14 and 1917–23.

JOHNSON, WILLIAM JOSEPH, O.B.E. (1927).—B. 1892; serv. in I.E.F., E. Africa, 1914–17; ment. in deaps., 1917; transf'd to depot, 111th Mahars, India, 1917; offr. in charge, clearing house, office of field contr. of mil'y. accts., E.E.F., Cairo, 1918; major, ch. accts. offr., O.E.T. admstr., Palestine, 1919; treas., Palestine civ. admstr., 1st July, 1920; dep. treas. on abolition of post of finan. sec., May, 1922; ag. treas. and mem. exec. and advisory couns., June to Sept., 1923, June to Sept., 1924, Jan., Apr. and May, 1925 and May to Sept., 1926; mem., comtees. on pub. security forces, 1923; mem., comtees. on establishment of permanent and pensionable cadre for gen. clerical serv., 1926; mem., road bd., 1926.

JOHNSTON, ALEXANDER.—B. 1867; ed. at pub. schls., and St. Francis Xavier Coll., Antigonish, Nova Scotia; entd. local legis. of Nova Scotia, April, 1897, as repres. for Cape Breton Co., Nova Scotia; resig., 1900; elec. to H. of C., 1900; re-elec., 1904; dep. min. marine and fisheries of Canada, June, 1910.

JOHNSTON, H. LINDSAY.—Govt. statist, S. Australia, 1916.

JOHNSTON, JOHN ROOKE.—B. 1894; ed. St. Ninians, Moffat and St. Bees Schls. and Sandhurst; 2nd lieut., The Black Watch, 23rd Dec., 1917; seconded to 2/1st K.A.R., 23rd Dec., 1920; adminis. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 12th Sept., 1923.

JOHNSTON, REGINALD FLEMING, C.M.G. (1928), C.B.E. (1918).—B. 1874; M.A. Magdalen Coll., Oxford (1901); Gray prizeman, Edin. Univ., 1894; prox. acc. Lord Rector's essay, Edin.; hors. in English lit., mod. hist. and constitutional law, Edin.; exhibr., Magd. Coll., Oxford, 1894; ment., hon. causa Stanhope Esmy, 1898; B.A., 1898; cadet, Hong Kong, 1898; ag. clk. of couns., 1899; priv. sec. to gov't., 1900–01; ag. ast. col. sec., 1900–04; J.P., June, 1902; sec. to gov't., Weihaiwei, 1904; dist. offr. and mag., ditto, 1906; seconded for serv. as tutor to Manchu Emperor (ex-King of China), 1919–26; read. from Emperor button of highest offl. grade and sable robe, 1922; warden, Summer Palace, Peking, 1924; brought Emperor into safety in legation quarter, Peking, Nov., 1924; sec. Br. China indemnity delegation, 1926; commr., Weihaiwei, 1927.

JOHNSTONE, ANGUS COLIN DUNCAN.—B. 1889; ed. Trin. Coll., Glenalmond, and in Germany; passed Army entrance exam., R.M.C., Sandhurst, 1908; higher grade staff, G. Cent. Rly., 1909–12; served, Balkan War, with Br. Red Cross Unit attd. Turkish Forces, 1912–13; lieut., 5th (Res.) Batt. West Yorks Regt. (T.), Nov., 1914 to Apr., 1915; ast. dist. commr., Gold Coast, 10th Sept., 1913; lieut., W.A.F.F., and attd. Gold Coast Regt., 23rd Apr., 1915; seconded Br. Forces, Togoland, May, 1915; offr., cls. II., polit. serv., 1st Jan., 1920; dist. commr., Ashanti Akim, 2nd Sept., 1922.

JOHNSTONE, BANNER CARRUTHERS.—B. 1882; ed. Eton and Trin. Coll., Camb.; B.A. (Cantab.); passed R.G.S. survey course, 1908; ast. supt., surveys, Ceylon, 21st Oct., 1909; ast. collr. (afterwards ast. dist. commr.), Zanzibar Prot., 23rd Apr., 1913; ag. 1st ast. sec. and clk. of coun., 16th Nov., 1914 to 11th June, 1915; ch. land attitl. offr., 1st Jan., 1916; seconded for active serv. in German East Africa, 13th Aug., 1916; on mil. serv., France, 30th Oct., 1916 to 7th Mar., 1919; ag. dist. commr., Pemba, 21st July, 1919 to 26th Apr., 1920; dist. commr., Pemba, 24th Nov., 1921; ag. senr. commr., 23rd Aug., 1924 to 22nd Feb., 1925; 3rd cls. Order of the Brilliant Star of Zanzibar, 1920; ag. senr. commr. from 26th Oct., 1926 to 17th Apr., 1927; mem., leg. coun.

JOHNSTONE, JAMES MONTAGUE CHOLMLEY.—Ent. prison dept. (England and Wales), Aug., 1921; dep. ast. supt., prisons, Trinidad, 1924; ast. supt., 1927.

JOHNSTONE, JOHN WILKIE.—B. 1884; solr., Eng'land, 1906; ast. polit. offr., G.E.A. (Tanganyika Territory), Nov., 1918; ag. mag., Apr., 1919 to Feb., 1921; called to bar, Gray's Inn, 1924.

JOHNSTONE, SIR ROBERT STEWART, KT. B.A. (1915).—Ed. at Trin. Coll., Dublin; B.A. (honors) and medal in history and political science),
1882; LL.B., 1884; M.A., 1895; Holt scholar, Gray's Inn, 1886; called to the Irish bar 1886; called to the bar at Gray's Inn, Jan., 1889; lieut., 3rd (Militia) Batt. Manchester Regt., 1883; capt., 1887; dist. comsnr., Lagos, 1889; served on Lagos and Porto Novo boundary comm., 1890; stip. and circuit mag. and judge of ct. of com. pleas, Bahamas, Jan., 1894; ag. atty.-gen., Aug. to Nov., 1902; oh. just., Grenada, 1909; ret., 1914.

JOMARON, ADOLPHE CHARLES.—B. 1893; ed. at University Coll. Schol. and Corpus Christi Coll., Camb. (class. schol.)—B.A. 1920; 2nd lieut., R.F.A., 1914; lieut., 1915; capt., 1917; ag. major, 1918; wounded, 1916; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1920; add. to asst. adviser's office, Muar, Johore; 2nd asst. adviser, Muar, Johore, Jan., 1922; passed cadet, June, 1922; offr., cls. V., June, 1922; seconded for serv. in Kelantan as ag. dist. offr., Pasir Puteh, July, 1923; ag. sup't., lands, Kelantan, asst. state andr., chmn., conservancy bd., Khota Bharu and coroner, June, 1924; offr., cls. IV., June, 1925; 3rd asst. sec. to govt., F.M.S., Nov., 1925; ag. temp. dist. offr., Larut and reglar. titles, Perak, Nov., 1927; sec. to rivers commnrs. in addn., Dec., 1927.

JONES, CHARLES BENJAMIN.—B. 1882; 6th cls. elk. treasy dept., S. Nigeria, 1905; 5th cls. elk., 1906; 4th cls. elk., div. comsnr.'s off., Bonny, 1906; prov. comsnr.'s off., E. Prov., 1906; 2nd cls. elk., Jan., 1907; head elk., sol. gen.'s off., E. Prov., Sept., 1909; istcls. elk., Jan., 1912.

JONES, CHARLES ERNEST.—B. 1892; B.A., B.Sc., Lond.; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1914; add. to Kegalla kach., Dec., 1914; Ratnapura kach., Apr., 1915; Kegalla kach., Jan., 1916; censor's off., Apr., 1916; on mily. duty, 1918; returned to censor's off., June, 1919; pol. mag., Matara, July, 1919; sec., retrenchment commn., Jan., 1923; addnl. asst. dir., educn., Dec., 1923; dist. judge, N'Ellya, Apr., 1926; asst. govt. agt., Mannar, Nov., 1926; asst. col. treas., Sept., 1928.

JONES, G. A.—B. 1889; appt., after compet. exam., elk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., Dec., 1907; asst. sec. to Oversea Prize Disposal Comm., Mar., 1917; ag. sec. to ditto, Jan., 1918; promoted under O.-in-C. of 1910, 2nd cls. elk., C.O., 14th Mar., 1919; prin., 1st Apr., 1920.

JONES, GWILYM ARTHUR.—Agric. diploma, Univ. Coll., Bangor, N. Wales, with 1st cls. in agric.; awarded Wm. Griffith prize, 1906-8; holder of certif. in forestry; ag. agric. and science master, Antigua gram. schl., 1909; asst. curator, botanic gardens, Dominica, Aug., 1909; in charge of agric. schl., Dominica, Aug., 1909, to Jan., 1910; asst. sec. to permanent exhibtn. comm., 1909; ag. curator, botanic gardens, Dominica, 1913; chemist, agric. dept., Dominica, Apr., 1915, and a director of the Victoria museum, 1915.

JONES, LLEWELLYN A. F.—Asst. dist. comsnr., R.A.P., 18th Dec., 1908; junr. asst. sec., Feb., 1912; priv. sec. to govt., 1915; dist. comsnr., June, 1916; ag. senr. comsnr., Kenya, 1926.

JONES, MALCOLM LUDLOW, O.B.E. (1919).—Served at Bd. of Trade (Labour Dept.), 1897-1901; chief elk., Emigrants' Information Office, 1901; visited Canada on behalf of E.I.O., 1907; chief elk., Oversea Settlem. Office, 1919.

JONES, CAPT. NELSON, M.C. (and Bar).—B. 1895; ed. Glasgow Univ.; comsdr., Cameron Highrs., 1915; M.C., Apr., 1917; bar, June, 1918; capt., July, 1918; discharged on account of wounds, Apr., 1919 cadet, F.M.S., Oct., 1919; asst. contr. of lab., Penang, Mar., 1920; asst. contr. of lab., K. Lumpur, May, 1921; on sp. duty in cust. dept. in connection with toddy shops, July, 1922; 2nd lieut., M.V.I., Nov., 1922; add. to dist. office, Klang, to act as 1st cls. mag., 1923; asst. dist. offr., Ulu Langat, July, 1924; 3rd mag., Singapore, July, 1924; ag. dep. contr., lab., Kuala Lumpur, May, 1925; ag. dep. contr., lab., Penang, July, 1925; ag. dep. contr., lab., Kedah, Jan., 1926.

JONES, PERCY SYDNEY TWENTYMAN.—B. 1876; ed. at Diocesan Coll., Rondebosch; White prize for classics; Archbishop's Greek testament prize; B.A., Cape, 1896; LL.B., Cape, 1898; called to bar, Aug., 1898; took silk, 1924; edited "Liquor Laws of Cape," and jointly with H. O. Buckle "Magistrates' Court Practice of S.A."; judge, Aug., 1926.

JONES, ROBERT NOBLE, C.B.E. (1928).—B. 1864; barrister and solr., N.Z., 1890; judge, native land ct. and dist. land regr., 1903; chief judge, native land ct., 1919; under sec., native dept., 1922.

JONES, SAMUEL BENJAMIN, M.B.E. (1924), M.A. (Durh.), B.A. (Lond.), Inter. LL.B. Exam. (Lond.), L.R.C.P., L.R.O.S., (Edin.), L.R.F.P.S. (Glasg.).—B. 1874; ed. Antigua Gram. Schl.; med. offr., and mag., Anguilla, 1918; thanked by exec. coun. of St. Kitts for checking outbreak of small pox in Anguilla, 1921; med. offr., dist. No. 2, St. Kitts, 1924.

JONES, STANLEY WILSON.—B. 1888; B.A. (Manchester), 1st cls. hon. hist. (1908); cadet, F.M.S., Dec., 1911; ag. asst. dist. offr., Pekan, June, 1912; passed cadet, Dec., 1913; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Lipis, Nov., 1914; offr., cls. V., Dec., 1914; ag. asst. dist. offr., Kuantan, Mar., 1916; ag. dist. offr., Pekan, Aug., 1917; asst. dist. offr., Kuala Kangsar, June, 1918; offr., cls. IV., Jan., 1919; dist. offr., Jelebu, Jan. 1920; dist. offr., Kuala Lipis, May, 1920; ag. dist. offr., Klang, Aug., 1923; ag. dist. offr., Kuantan, Sept., 1923; local examr. in law and Malay, Nov., 1923; offr., cls. III., Dec., 1923; add. to federal secretariat on sp. duty, Aug., 1924; local examr. in Malay, Selangor, Sept., 1924; ag. comsnr., trade and cust., Johore, Dec., 1927.

JONES, WILLIAM JOHN ANDREW, B.A. (Oxford).—B. 1889; ed. Jesus Coll., Oxford; asst. dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, 26th Mar., 1913; dist. comsnr., 18th Dec., 1918; dep. prov. comsnr., 3rd Jan., 1924.

JONES, W. PATRICK.—Impl. service, 1891 to 1902; elk., treasy., Transvaal, 18th Mar., 1902; priv. sec. to col. treas., Apr., 1903; principal elk., treasy., 1st July, 1904; principal elk., dept. of finance, U. of S. Africa, 1910; chief elk., treasy., Union of S. Africa, 1st Aug., 1912; chief elk. and acctnt., in rev. dept., Mar., 1917; ch. survr. of rev., 1st Nov., 1921; recr. rev., Johannesburg, Dec., 1923.

JONES-BATEMAN, REGINALD.—B. 1894; on mil. serv., Sept., 1914; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1919; attached to Kurunegala Kach., Dec., 1919; office asst. to supt. of census and dir. of statistics, Oct., 1921; pol. mag., Jaffna, Oct., 1924; asst. govt. agt., Mullattivu, Nov., 1924; asst. govt. agt., Kandy, Dec., 1926; asst. stlitm. offr., Aug., 1927.

JORDAN, ARTHUR BENJAMIN.—B. 1890; ed. Nottingham High Schl., and Jesus Coll., Oxford (class. exhib.)—B.A., Oxon., 1913; cadet, F.M.S., 28th Nov., 1913; passed final exam. in Cantonese, 26th Apr., 1916; ag. asst. contr. of
lab., K. Lumpur, 6th June, 1916; 2nd lieut., Malayan Vol. Infy., 6th Dec., 1916; passed F.M.S. govt. exam. in law, and passed cadet, 20th Dec., 1916; offr., cls. V, offtrg. as asst. contr. of lab., K. Lumpur, 26th Dec., 1916; ag. prot. of Chinese, Perak, 30th Nov., 1917; asst. contr. of lab., K. Lumpur, 15th Jan., 1918; lieut., Malayan Vol. Infy., 6th Dec., 1918; asst. dist. offr., Raub (Bentong), 28th Feb., 1919; offr., cls. IV, 28th Nov., 1920; asst. prot. of Chinese, Negri Sembilan, 15th Apr., 1921; ag. prot., Chinese, Perak, Dec., 1923; ag. prot., Chinese, Selangor and Pahang, Apr., 1925; offr., cls. III, Nov., 1925; prot., Chinese, Negri Sembilan, Oct., 1926; ag. asst. chmn., sayn. bd., Kinta, Mar., 1927.

JORDAN, A. H.—B. 1903; ent. C.O., 17th Mar., 1919; cler. offr., 14th Oct., 1921.

JOY, GEORGE ANDREW.—B. 1896; ed. St. Francis Xavier's Coll., Bruges; ent. Army, 1914; served in Belgium and France, 1915 and 1916; Palestine and Syria, 1917-18; staff gen. headqrs., Egypt and Palestine, 1919-20; S.W. Arabia, 1921 to 1923; ment. in desps., lieut., R.A.R.O., Feb., 1919; asst. to res. comsrr., New Hebrides, Aug., 1924; dep. comsrr., W. Pacific, 8th July, 1926; ag. Br. res. comsrr., 18th Aug., 1927; res. comsrr., New Hebrides, 1928.

JOYCE, G. F. W. C.—B. 1897; ent. R.I.O., June, 1912; asst. clk., Jan., 1915; on mily. serv., Sept., 1914 to Apr., 1919; cler. offr., O.S.O., 1st Jan., 1920.

JOYCE, BREVET LIEUT.-COL. PIERCE CHARLES, C.B.E. (1920), D.S.O. (1918).—B. 1878; ed. Beaumont Coll., Old Windsor; joined 1st Batt. The Connaught Rangers, 1900; serv. S. African War, 1900-02 (severely wounded, Queen's Med. with 3 claps, King's Med. with 2 claps); attd., Egyptian Army, 1907-16 (Egyptian Med. with clap, 4th cls., Order of the Medjidieh, 4th cls., Order of the Nile); European War, 1915 (Gallipoli); Arab campaign against the Turks, 1916-18; mily. advr. to Amir Faisal, 1917 (ment. in desps. five times, brevet of lieut.-col., C.B.E., D.S.O., Croix d'Officier, Legion of Honour, Arabian Order of the Nakhshid, 2nd cls.); gov., E. and S. Desert Provs., Egypt, 1920; mil. adviser to Iraq Govt., Mar., 1921.

JOYNT, HENRY RAYMOND, B.A.—B. 1888; ed. Bradfield and Balliol Coll., Oxford (math. schol.); cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1911; ag. 2nd asst. contr. of lab., Penang, Mar., 1913; ag. asst. contr. of lab., K. Lumpur, Apr., 1914; passed cadet, July, 1914; ag. rev. audr., Sel. N. Sembilan and Phg., June, 1918; dist. offr., K. Langat, Nov., 1919; dep. contr. of lab., Seremban, Mar., 1921; agt. to food contr., N. Sembilan in addn., Apr. to July, 1921; ag. dep. contr., lab., Penang, Nov., 1921; ag. contr., lab., in addition, Apr., 1922 on sp. duty, rubber census office, Kuala Lumpur, June, 1922; ag. 2nd asst. sec., gov't. of F.M.S., Nov., 1923; offr., cls. III., Nov., 1923; second asst. sec. to gov't., F.M.S., Nov., 1923; ag. mag., Kuala Lumpur, Sept., 1927; ag. collr., estate duty, F.M.S., Dec., 1927; ag. offl. assignee and pub. trustee, F.M.S. in addn., June 1928.

JUSTICE, SIR HARTMANN W., K.C.M.G. (1911), C.B. (1902), C.M.G. (1900), B.A. (1877).—B. 1854; appointed, after compet. exam., clk. in office of sec. of state for the col., 3rd June, 1875; ed. at Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford; was an open scholar on the foundation; 1st class in classical mods., 1874; Taylorian exhibitioner for German, 1876; 2nd class in final classical school, 1877; asst. priv. sec. to the late Earl of Derby, 6th Feb., 1883, to Col. F. A. Stanley (now Earl of Derby), 24th June, 1885, and to Mr. Stanhope, 3rd Aug., 1886; priv. sec. to Mr. Osborne Morgan, 6th Feb. to 3rd Aug., 1886; asst. priv. sec. to Sir H. Holland (afterwards Viscount Knutsford), 12th Jan., 1887, and to the Marquess of Ripon, 17th Aug., 1892; asst. sec. to the col. confce., 1887; 1st class clk., Apr., 1895; prin. clk., Mar., 1897; accompanied Rt. Hon. Joseph Chamberlain on his visit to S. Africa, 1902-3; asst. under-sec. of state, Jan., 1907; jt. sec. to Imp. Confce., 1907; sec. to Imp. Confce. on naval and mil. defence, 1909; visited Canada, 1910; also Australia and New Zealand, 1914; permanent sec. to Imp. Confce.; regisr. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George; represented C.O. on advisory comtees. of comm. intell., B. of T.; retired, 1916.

JUTA, CARL WILHELM THALMAN BICCAED.—B. 1872; ed. at S.A. Coll., Cape Town; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1898; advoc., sup. ct., 1899; state atty.'s office, Transvaal, 1899; ch. clk., Transvaal patent office, 1902; asst. regisr., companies, 1904; comsrr., patents and regisr., companies, Transvaal, 1908; regisr., patents, designs, trade marks, copyright, Union of S. Africa, 1st Jan., 1917; del. to Empire patent confce., 1922; regisr. of companies for Union of S. Africa, 1st Jan., 1927.
